title: Suggestions - review before implementing
description: A dedicated review queue of proposed improvements to this site and to the rent-increase decision process. Each suggestion states what it changes, why it helps, the official basis, the effort, and its review status so a reviewer can choose the best path before anything is implemented.

sections.title: How to use this page (the review process)

rows.label: 1. Read the proposal
rows.value: Each suggestion below states the exact change, the decision it improves, and the official source that motivates it. Nothing is implemented by being listed here.
rows.notes: Honest label: this is a proposal queue, not a change log.

rows.label: 2. Check the evidence
rows.value: Open the linked official page and confirm the quoted rule, dollar figure or date still says what the row says. If it does not, the suggestion is stale - say so before accepting it.
rows.notes: Every row on this site is linked for exactly this reason.

rows.label: 3. Choose a path
rows.value: Accept, defer or decline. Accepting a suggestion is a decision by the owner (or by the next build session for site-only changes). No suggestion here changes a legal obligation on its own.
rows.notes: Nothing auto-applies.

rows.label: 4. Record the outcome
rows.value: Write the decision, the date and the reviewer in the review-status column (or in COORDINATION.md), so the next session does not re-litigate a closed item.
rows.notes: COORDINATION.md is the shared task board for this repository.

rows.label: 5. Only then implement
rows.value: Implementation means editing scripts/site_*.py and rebuilding, not hand-editing pages. The validator re-runs every check after a build.
rows.notes: Generated files are reproducible; CI re-runs the build and fails on drift.

rows.label: 6. Record the choice in section D
rows.value: Section D is the decision record. Every row there is deliberately blank: this page lists options, evidence and effort, and does not choose for you. A choice written down with a date is what stops a later review re-opening an item that was already settled.
rows.notes: Added 2026-11-13 so the review has somewhere to land; nothing on this page is implemented by being listed.

sections.title: A. Suggestions to close information gaps before deciding

rows.label: Pull the Property Information Map record for both units and record the official build year, unit count and any in-law designation
rows.value: The owner-stated 1940 year and two-unit count are the entire basis for assuming coverage. If the official record shows a post-1979 certificate of occupancy or a single-family designation, the whole licensing analysis changes. This is the single highest-value open item.
rows.notes: Maps to CASE-V1 / CASE-V2. Owner action; the agent cannot log in.

rows.label: Log in to the Rent Board Portal and screenshot the Housing Inventory status and licence status for each unit
rows.value: Licence status is the one unverified fact that can void an entire increase under Rule 13.14. Everything downstream depends on it.
rows.notes: Maps to CASE-V3 / T03-F05.

rows.label: Reconstruct the actual rent history for each unit from leases, bank statements and any prior notices
rows.value: Banked increases are the only lawful route above 1.6%, and they can only be computed from a real payment history. Without it, every banked figure on this site stays blank - correctly.
rows.notes: Maps to CASE-V4 / CASE-V9, flag F30.

rows.label: Identify, in writing, the legal status of the occupant added to Unit 1 on April 1, 2026 (co-tenant, subtenant or assignee) and whether a written Section 6.14 notice was served
rows.value: Co-tenant status means no market reset at all; subtenant/assignee status could allow one only with specific facts and a timely written notice. The difference is large and it is a fact question, not a research question.
rows.notes: Maps to CASE-V5 to CASE-V8, flag F28.

rows.label: Ask the Rent Board directly (311 or 415-252-4600) whether the April 1, 2026 continuation restarted the Annex A / anniversary clock
rows.value: The anniversary date determines the earliest lawful effective date. A wrong assumption here makes an otherwise compliant notice premature.
rows.notes: Maps to CASE-V6. Free counselling; not legal advice.

rows.label: Get one paid hour with a tenant-side or landlord-tenant attorney to review the completed Notice Worksheet
rows.value: Every page here says the same thing: this is a compliance checklist capable of review, not an approval. A single review converts an open question into a documented position.
rows.notes: Maps to F47 / REQ-21. The site never claims attorney approval.

rows.label: Confirm the Rent Board Fee exemption status and billing record for both units
rows.value: The fee is a separate obligation with penalties up to 15%; whether it has been paid or exempted is unverified and is independently enforceable.
rows.notes: Maps to FEE-12 / F43.

sections.title: B. Suggestions to improve this site so it supports a decision

rows.label: Add a printable one-page decision sheet that lists only the eight gate questions and the owner-stated answers
rows.value: The full site is comprehensive but too long to use at the moment of deciding. A one-pager is what a reviewer actually holds while checking a draft notice.
rows.notes: New file; does not alter any verified value.

rows.label: Add an automated 'stale source' check that re-fetches every official URL on a schedule and flags any page whose quoted figure changed
rows.value: The 1.6% rate, the $59.00 fee and File 261020 all move. A dated diff is the cheapest defence against relying on an out-of-date page.
rows.notes: Would require a scheduled workflow; currently sources are re-checked manually per session.

rows.label: Link each flag directly from the table cell that raised it, in both directions
rows.value: Reviewers currently read a row, then hunt the flag. Bidirectional links cut review time and reduce the chance a flagged row is acted on as if it were verified.
rows.notes: Improves navigation only; no content change.

rows.label: Publish a diff-style change log of every figure that changed between builds
rows.value: Re-verification is only meaningful if a reader can see what moved. A visible changelog makes an auditor's job possible without reading git history.
rows.notes: Git history already contains the data; this only surfaces it.

rows.label: Add a plain-language glossary (base rent, anniversary date, banked increase, passthrough, license, Housing Inventory)
rows.value: Several terms look interchangeable to a first-time owner but carry different legal consequences - notably license vs fee, and banked increase vs passthrough.
rows.notes: Definitions must be quoted from the official pages, not paraphrased freely.

rows.label: Keep the site free of any owner name, address or tenant identifier, and re-run the privacy check on every build
rows.value: Privacy is the owner's stated top priority, and the F44/F51 history flags show how easily identifiers leak into a public repository.
rows.notes: F44 and F51 remain owner-actionable for historical commits; this site cannot rewrite published history.

sections.title: C. Suggestions on how to approach the increase itself (decision paths, not legal advice)

rows.label: Adopt one written, neutral rule - 'on each unit's anniversary date, impose the published annual allowable increase if the licence is current' - and apply it identically to both units
rows.value: An identical rule applied by anniversary date is the cleanest answer to the one-vs-both discrimination question, because the selection criterion is the calendar, not the tenant.
rows.notes: Analysis recommendation. It is not a guarantee against a complaint or a petition.

rows.label: Document the neutral reason for any unit that is NOT increased at the same time (for example: anniversary not reached, or licence not current)
rows.value: If the two units are treated differently, the file should show a reason that does not depend on who the tenant is. This is the practical defence in a disparate-treatment inquiry.
rows.notes: Contingent recommendation; depends on SUG-A2 and SUG-A5.

rows.label: Do not raise rent merely because a roommate was added to Unit 1
rows.value: SF.gov states additional-occupant charges are an unlawful rent increase even where the lease provides for one. This is the sharpest available trap in this case.
rows.notes: Directly answers Q-14 and AN-07.

rows.label: Set the effective date no earlier than the later of (a) the anniversary date and (b) the date the licence is confirmed on file
rows.value: Rule 13.14 tests the effective date, not the service date. Sequencing the dates this way removes the nullity risk without needing to guess.
rows.notes: Conservative sequencing; the rule states the legal test, the sequence is the recommendation.

rows.label: Serve the notice with proof of service and keep a dated copy of the official pages relied on
rows.value: A dated record is the cheapest way to answer a later question about which rate and which rules were in force when the notice was served.
rows.notes: Matches the existing Notice Worksheet (pages/worksheet.html).

rows.label: Re-check File 261020's committee status immediately before serving any banked or capital-improvement notice
rows.value: The pending ordinance targets exactly the stacked multi-year increase that Unit 2's long tenure could theoretically support. It is not law today, but that can change.
rows.notes: Maps to F46 / REQ-25.

sections.title: D. Owner decision record - blank until you choose (the site takes no position)
columns: Your decision - blank until the owner records it
What is being decided, and what to write in the decision column

rows.label: Which annual rate to apply
rows.notes: Decides SUG-C4 and every amount row on the site: the rate in force on the increase's EFFECTIVE date (1.6% for 3/1/26-2/28/27) versus waiting for the next published rate. The 2027-28 figure is not yet published (F27), so it cannot be planned around. Record here: the effective date you chose, the rate you used, and the date you confirmed it on the official page.

rows.label: One unit or both
rows.notes: Decides SUG-C1 and SUG-C2. Options: both units on their own anniversary dates under one written neutral rule; Unit 1 only; Unit 2 only; neither this cycle. No official source requires both and none forbids one - the exposure is in the reason and the record, not the count. Record here: the choice, and the neutral rule applied to reach it, written before any notice goes out.

rows.label: Whether to pursue a banked increase at all
rows.notes: Decides SUG-A3. Options: no banked claim (1.6% only, the documented default); reconstruct the history from leases, notices and payment records and bank what is provable; or stop and get advice first. No banked amount is asserted for either unit on this site (F30). Record here: the decision, and if a banked claim is pursued, the documents relied on and who checked them.

rows.label: Whether to spend the attorney hour before serving
rows.notes: Decides SUG-A6. Options: review the completed Notice Worksheet with counsel before service; review afterwards; or rely on self-review. This is the one item on the board a third party can close for you. Record here: yes or no, the date, and the questions asked.

rows.label: Which site improvements to build
rows.notes: Decides the SUG-B group (one-page decision sheet, stale-source re-check, bidirectional flag links, change log, glossary, privacy guard). Site-only rows can be accepted by the owner or by the next build session; accepting one changes no legal obligation. Record here: the IDs you accept, in priority order, and who should build them.

rows.label: Privacy remediation of the repository history
rows.notes: Decides SUG-B6 and flags F44/F51. Raw tenant identifiers remain reachable in commits and closed pull-request diffs on this public repository. Options: rewrite history and force-push; delete and re-create the repository; close the stale pull requests and accept the exposure; or take the repository private. Only the owner can do any of these. Record here: the choice and the date it was done, so the flags can be closed against an action instead of left open indefinitely.

rows.label: Whether to use a petition route above 1.6%
rows.notes: Decides the petition questions on the Reasons and Process pages. Options: no petition; a capital-improvement or O&M petition, which must be FILED BEFORE the notice is served or the notice is void; or a documented passthrough, which needs no licence but is a different kind of increase. Each has its own worksheet, cost and timing. Record here: the route chosen, whether a petition was filed, and its file number and date.

rows.label: Whether to increase anything this cycle
rows.notes: The last option, and sometimes the right one: if coverage (SUG-A1), licence status (SUG-A2) or an open repair/retaliation question cannot be closed, doing nothing costs nothing, and the right to bank accrues while 24 full months pass without an increase. Record here: the decision to defer, the reason, and the date to re-check.
